title: A smart wristwatch prompts a patient's readmission to the emergency department for investigation and management of a postoperative pulmonary embolism (Toronto, JBJS Case Connector 2021)
summary: Toronto Western Hospital orthopedic surgeons report a smart wristwatch prompting ED readmission for postoperative pulmonary embolism investigation and management; only the abstract could be read.
account: Drynan, Leroux and Zywiel of the Division of Orthopedic Surgery, Toronto Western Hospital, University of Toronto, reported in JBJS Case Connector (volume 11, issue 2, April-June 2021; published online 8 June 2021, which is used as the date because the event date is not available) a case in which, in the abstract's words, a smart wristwatch prompted a patient's readmission to the emergency department for postoperative pulmonary embolism investigation and management. The abstract adds that constant patient monitoring and alerts are advantages of community-based smart technology and that surrounding issues must be considered in implementation. Only the abstract could be read: the full text is behind the LWW/Ovid paywall, no PMC or Wayback copy exists, and an earlier check also had abstract only. The patient's age, sex, operation, what the watch measured or alerted, the device's brand, and the clinical outcome are therefore not known.
purpose: Consumer activity monitors are built to track heart rate and activity and to alert the wearer; the abstract credits the watch with prompting the readmission but does not say which function did so.
system: Smart wristwatch / personal activity monitor (brand, model and alert type not stated in the abstract)
developer: Not stated (the abstract does not name the device's maker)
location: Toronto, Canada (authors' institution; the abstract does not state where the case occurred)

ratings.reason: The abstract states that the watch prompted the patient's readmission for postoperative pulmonary embolism investigation and management, a serious condition caught in time; the outcome is not detailed, and only the abstract could be read.

ai_role.statement: Only the abstract was readable. It credits a smart wristwatch with prompting the readmission and refers to monitoring and alerts, but does not say what the device measured, whether an automatic alert fired, or what brand or algorithm was involved, so the device's contribution cannot be assessed.
